validation.focused_coverage: Noinline dynamic integer inputs, signed boundaries, seeded random words, wrapping products, 12 simultaneously live products, and actual LEA selection on x86-64.

in_place.decision: Not accepted: retains the input move and did not show a clear runtime gain.
in_place.patch:
diff --git a/core/compiler/x64.jo b/core/compiler/x64.jo
index 4702fa01..6232d10c 100644
--- a/core/compiler/x64.jo
+++ b/core/compiler/x64.jo
@@ -1739,10 +1739,19 @@ emit_ins = (pos: int, ins: Ins):
             l = vloc[bb]
             if l == LOC_CONST:
                 c = vcval[bb]
-                rex(true, r, 0, r, false)
-                b(0x69)
-                modrr(r, r)
-                b32(c)
+                if c == 3 or c == 5 or c == 9:
+                    # x + x * {2,4,8}, preserving the same low 64 bits.
+                    scale = 1
+                    if c == 5: scale = 2
+                    else if c == 9: scale = 3
+                    use_index(r, scale)
+                    lea(r, r, 0)
+                    cur_index = -1
+                else:
+                    rex(true, r, 0, r, false)
+                    b(0x69)
+                    modrr(r, r)
+                    b32(c)
             else:
                 rb = reg_of(bb, RCX)
                 rex(true, r, 0, rb, false)

measurement_notes: All initial and focused matched samples are retained. Rechecks cover only unresolved stage comparisons.

The original stage report retains its original C ratios from separate medians. The final assessment reprocesses the retained matched samples with the corrected C comparison, including fresh matched release/C recheck samples. No timing results are invented or copied from an earlier stage.
Three workloads match the accepted artifacts and use runtime certificates with fresh checks; changed artifacts receive new timing samples. Unmeasured C ratios remain null.
Host load changed sharply during this run. Separate medians of compiler timings can diverge despite flat paired ratios; do not interpret the new absolute throughput as a compiler-only gain.
The fresh root-source throughput target of 250k lines/s and broad C/Rust runtime goal remain unmet.
